nodes.name: Slack Gateway Webhook
nodes.notes: Bind a Header Auth credential whose Name is exactly 'Authorization' and whose Value is 'Bearer <ORCHESTRATOR_SHARED_SECRET>'. slack_bot._forward sends that one header and no custom gateway header, so any other header name rejects the orchestrator's own caller. 'Ignore Bots' is deliberately OFF: the caller is python-httpx, which user-agent bot filters can classify as a bot and drop before authentication.

nodes.name: Relay To Orchestrator
nodes.notes: Pass-through relay, not a normalizer. slack_bot._forward already builds the canonical SlackIntake (source_event_id, channel_id, thread_ts, user_id, text, allocation_profile, primary_required_capabilities, permalink, received_at), HMAC-signs it, and posts it here. The body is forwarded unchanged: SlackIntake sets extra='forbid', and the attestation in approvals._slack_intake_attestation_payload covers intake.model_dump(mode='json'), so adding, dropping, or regenerating any field breaks validation, the signature, or both. allocation_profile is owner-set deployment configuration and must never be injected here. The three X-Director-Intake-* headers are forwarded because verify_slack_intake_attestation requires them once ALLOW_PAID_RUNS is true; they are empty and unused while it is false. source_event_id is the idempotency key: re-delivery creates no second task.

nodes.name: Accepted
nodes.notes: The orchestrator's TaskRecord is returned verbatim. slack_bot._intake_receipt_task_id requires one task_id matching DIR-(LG-)?[A-F0-9]+ at the top level or under data, and _forward additionally requires HTTP 202 exactly. A summarised or renamed body makes the bot post 'DIRECTOR - BLOCKED' on a successful intake.

nodes.name: Intake Failed
nodes.notes: A non-2xx from /v1/intake must not return 200 or 202. Only the upstream status code is echoed; no response body, provider output or secret-shaped value is relayed.
